claims.text: The University of Edinburgh does not ban generative AI in postgraduate research, but its use is restricted for assessed work; researchers should consult supervisors and programme-level guidelines, should include a brief acknowledgment in the Declaration of Own Work if using AI for assessed research, and must adhere to publisher and funder rules.

evidence.quote:
The University does not ban the use of generative AI in your research, though its use is restricted for work assessed by the University.
Some programmes and disciplines may also restrict its use in other ways. Always check with your supervisors and any programme-level guidelines.
If you are considering using generative AI for research in conference papers, posters and publications, you should also consult any guidelines provided by the conference organiser or publisher and make any appropriate declarations.
If you are a funded student, check whether your funder stipulates any additional restrictions.

claims.text: GenAI permissions at Edinburgh are set at assessment and course level; restrictions should be stated in the assessment task and students must consult their Course Organiser when unclear.

evidence.quote:
Before using GenAI in any assessed work, please check whether there are any restrictions.
This should be mentioned in the assessment task. If not, then ask your Course Organiser.
Some assessments may explicitly ask you to work with AI tools and to analyse and critique
the content it generates. Other assessments may specify, for good reason, that AI tools
should not be used in particular ways.

additionalTopics.summary: 系统性或大规模的非科研 AI 引入，以及将 AI 加入现有平台，应经 ISG 伦理委员会审批并完成所需影响评估；DPIA／EQIA 在适当或规定情形下完成。科研 AI 使用则遵循学院研究伦理委员会流程。
additionalTopics.scope: 系统性或大规模非科研引入及平台集成；科研伦理另循学院流程。
actions: Use the ISG Ethics Board process for the stated non-research scope.
Complete DPIA/EQIA where appropriate or required.
For research, follow the College Research Ethics Board process.

claims.text: For systematic or large-scale non-research adoption of AI or introduction of AI into existing platforms, staff must follow the approval process via the ISG Ethics Board, frame decisions using AI Impact Assessment guidance, and complete required impact assessments, including DPIA (Data Protection Impact Assessment) and EQIA (Equality Impact Assessment) where appropriate / as required (while research AI uses follow College Research Ethics Boards).

evidence.quote:
Many vendors are adding AI features to existing software. Treat these as new capabilities that require governance. Do not enable them by default. For systematic or large-scale adoption (including AI in third-party apps or the introduction of AI into an existing platform) for non-research activities, follow the approval process via the ISG Ethics Board, and complete required impact assessments. For Research use of AI follow your normal College Research Ethics Board process. Consider using the AI Impact Assessment guidance to frame decisions, and complete, where appropriate: Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA)
Equality Impact Assessment (EQIA)
